prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: sideswipe while changing lanes in League City, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1306; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd prefer to keep my name off the record for now, since I've been told the transcript goes into the court file. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: That's fine. Where were you on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving north on the frontage road in League City, Texas, heading toward a medical appointment I had that morning.

Q: Walk me through what happened as you remember it.

A: Traffic was moderate. I was in the middle lane and I noticed the car on my right was drifting. I honked and tried to move slightly left, but the other vehicle changed lanes into my side. The impact pushed my car toward the median. I grabbed the wheel with both hands and that's when I felt my right wrist give out.

Q: Did you stop after the impact?

A: Yes, I pulled onto the shoulder. The other driver stopped a few car lengths ahead. We exchanged information and a police officer came to file a report.

Q: Did you seek medical care right away?

A: An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They took X-rays and told me the wrist was fractured. They put it in a splint and referred me to an orthopedic specialist.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?

A: I had a follow-up visit where they confirmed the fracture was displaced, so I needed a cast for several weeks. After that I started physical therapy twice a week. My therapist has me doing grip exercises and range-of-motion work at home too.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: Pretty significantly. I'm right-handed, so simple things like buttoning a shirt, cutting food, or typing take much longer. I had to hand my grocery bags to my husband because I couldn't carry them. I also stopped going to my weekly pottery class because I couldn't hold the tools.

Q: Have you returned to work?

A: I've gone back in a limited capacity. My job involves a lot of computer work, and for the first few weeks I could only manage short stretches at the keyboard. My employer has been accommodating, but I've lost some hours.

Q: Do you still have pain today?

A: Yes. It's worse when the weather changes and after I've used the wrist for a long time. Some mornings I wake up stiff and it takes a while to loosen up.
